surfaces.part: top light band of upper housing
beer glass in the recessed tray, with a white rim band

answer.evidence: The upper housing has a light band in rows 3-6 (L 244 to 202, fading downward). It ends in a slightly darker line at row 6, and a blue shadow stripe at rows 7-8 sits beneath it. The gray front face with the nozzle runs from row 9 down, and the whole object has about 23 rows of front face. The top band is only 4 rows and could also be read as a white label panel. I treat it as a weak top surface, since the stripe works like an eave shadow. The lower red panel (rows 25-30) is a pure vertical face with no top, which is why all_major_parts_have_top is false. The silhouette widens from 14 to 16 px at row 16 around the beer tray.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a small, roughly one-tile-wide appliance prop. Its measured facts are close to the richer references. It has 15 visible tones per 16x16 tile, against 17 for the cheese stall, 20 for the roofed well and 9 for the hedge. Near-flat coverage is 0%, so there are no big flat fills. Dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the outline leans to the material tone (blue-grey on the body, brown on the base) and is not a sticker-style black line. The body, panel and mug show about 4 lightness steps each, a little under Beodeul's 5-6. The total palette of 20 colours is also well below the stall's 40 and the well's 38. Texture is limited to a few dots and highlights, with no real grain. A careful artist would still accept it next to the references, though it is slightly lighter on detail than the stall and well.

surfaces.part: top cap of the server body

answer.evidence: Rows 3-6 form a light band across the full body width. It shades from L=244 down to 202 at row 6, which reads as a front-edge line. A blue stripe in rows 7-8 below it acts as eave shadow. The grey front face with the spout runs from row 9 down to row 31, 25 rows in all. The top is a borderline 4-row band. It could also be a front-facing panel with a blue accent stripe, but the edge line and the shadow stripe below it count as evidence (a). The mug section (rows 16-23) and the red drip-tray panel (rows 24-31) are drawn face-on with no horizontal surface, so not every part shows a top.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a small standing prop, about one tile wide and a bit over one tile tall, so it is comparable to the lamp and bench. The measured facts are at or near the references: 15 visible tones per tile against 9 for the hedge, 17 for the cheese stall and 20 for the well. Near-flat coverage is 0%, and none of the dark edge pixels are neutral, so the outline carries a tint (dark blue-grey beside the casing, dark brown beside the mug) rather than a uniform black line. By eye the casing shows a highlight, a mid tone and a shadow side, with a separate blue cap and a gold beer mug, so there are no large flat fills. It is a little simpler than the richer references: about 4 steps on the body ramp and only 20 total colours, against 38-40 for the stall and well. That is slightly lower density but acceptable for a small appliance-like prop, and it does not look like a sticker next to the references.
